prompt: Will the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield (FRED DGS10 official daily) print at or above 5.00% on any observation through Friday 23 Oct 2026 12:00 PM CT?
editorial_note: We picked this contract because duration risk—and the buyers who must own it—is live on our Overton board right now. The 10-year yield is the market's single best gauge of term premium and fiscal-stress pricing; 5.00% is a clean, publicly checkable round number that sits comfortably above the Sep 2 print of 4.79%. We pinned expiry to Oct 23 because that date aligns with the TY futures options serial cycle, not the Oct 16 Friday weekly.
expires_rule: Resolves Friday 2026-10-23 12:00 PM CT — settlement by FRED DGS10 observation date (not a noon clock print)

resolution_clarity.source_of_truth: FRED series DGS10 (10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate, official daily)
resolution_criteria: YES if any official DGS10 daily observation with observation date on or before 2026-10-23 has a value greater than or equal to 5.00.
The 12:00 PM America/Chicago clock on 2026-10-23 closes which observation dates are in scope; it does not require FRED to publish at noon.
Use the observation date on the series, not the retrieval timestamp.
If FRED later revises a print, use the value as published for that observation date at resolution time.

sides.a: Affirmative (YES, DGS10 prints at or above 5.00% by Oct 23)
sides.b: Negative (NO, DGS10 stays below 5.00% through Oct 23)

argument_requirements: Both sides must distinguish DGS10 constant-maturity yield from the on-the-run 10-year cash note and TY futures when discussing price levels, spreads, and market mechanics.

Both sides must weigh auction dynamics, Treasury refunding calendar, foreign demand, and SLR-captivity pressures against soft-landing narratives and the Fed's expected rate path, without treating either as determinative.
Both sides must treat the 5.00% level as a concrete print rule—does DGS10 touch or exceed 5.00 on any observation date by Oct 23?—not a directional vibes call or investment recommendation.

evidence_brief.fact: The contract resolves YES if any official FRED DGS10 daily observation with observation date on or before 2026-10-23 prints at or above 5.00%. The window is approximately seven weeks.
evidence_brief.limitation: This is the contract rule, not market data.

evidence_brief.fact: On September 2, 2026, the FRED DGS10 series printed 4.79%.
evidence_brief.source: FRED DGS10 (10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate)
evidence_brief.limitation: Briefing anchor supplied by Ditka; confirm on FRED before publish.

evidence_brief.fact: The contract expiry of October 23, 2026 is pinned to the TY futures options serial expiration cycle, not the October 16 Friday weekly options. This aligns settlement with the deeper, more liquid options structure.
evidence_brief.source: CME Group Treasury futures options calendar
evidence_brief.limitation: Scheduling note for contract design; not a trade recommendation.
